derivations.claim: Since $D$ is nonempty and open it contains a ball, while boundedness gives finite measure; thus $0<|D|<\infty$ and $1\in L^2(D)$. [F3] therefore makes $\int_Dg\,dx$ finite. For $q\in Q$, [F3] gives $|S_g(q)|\le\|g\|_2\|q\|_2$, so $S_g\in Q'$. Also $g-\bar g\in Q$ and $S_g(q)-S_{g-\bar g}(q)=\bar g\int_Dq\,dx=0$; hence the normalized-gauge sensor depends only on the mean-zero part of $g$.

Under the Countable Choice assumption [A1], apply [F2]: every $v\in V$ has $\operatorname{div}v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ and $\int_D\operatorname{div}v\,dx=0$. Since $D$ has finite measure, $p+c\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ and [F3] makes both pressure pairings finite. Their difference is $-c\int_D\operatorname{div}v\,dx=0$, so adding a constant leaves the weak pressure term unchanged.

For any $p\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ and $c\in\mathbb R$, boundedness of $D$ gives $p+c\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$, and [F3] makes both sensor pairings finite. Their difference is $\int_Dg(p+c)\,dx-\int_Dgp\,dx=c\int_Dg\,dx$. If $\int_Dg=0$, every shift leaves the reading unchanged; conversely, invariance for every shift, in particular $c=1$, forces $\int_Dg=0$. By the definition of $Q$, this is equivalent to $g\in Q$.

A bounded Stokes pressure sensor on $D$ is a bounded real-linear functional $S:Q\to\mathbb R

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open set, with $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$. Take $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ and define $S_g(q):=\int_Dgq\,dx$ for $q\in Q$; this is a bounded pressure sensor. Put $\bar g:=|D|^{-1}\int_Dg\,dx$. On the normalized pressure space, $S_g=S_{g-\bar g}$. Whenever $p$ denotes an unnormalized pressure representative in a weak pressure term or sensor reading below, take $p\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$; a normalized pressure is denoted $q\in Q\subset L^2(D;\mathbb R)$. The weak Stokes pressure term $-\int_Dp\,\operatorname{div}v\,dx$ is unchanged by $p\mapsto p+c$ for $v\in V$ and $c\in\mathbb R$. The unnormalized sensor reading $\int_Dgp\,dx$ is unchanged under every pressure shift $p\mapsto p+c$ if and only if $\int_Dg\,dx=0$, equivalently $g\in Q$.
